title: Rajkumar Hirani Has Never Made a Flop. His First Streaming Show Just Dropped Its Trailer.
excerpt: 'Pritam and Pedro' brings the man behind 3 Idiots and Munna Bhai to JioHotstar on July 3 — with Arshad Warsi back in the fold, a debutant son, and Vikrant Massey playing the villain for once.
body:
The trailer opens on a beach in Goa, and there is an ATM machine sitting in the sand where no ATM machine has any business being. By the time you've finished asking yourself how it got there, Arshad Warsi has wandered into frame in a rumpled cop's uniform, looking like a man who has been demoted one too many times — and the warmth hits you before the plot does. This is what a Rajkumar Hirani production feels like. You don't watch it so much as get welcomed into it.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=uCjkRVV0-qU

On Monday, JioHotstar released the full trailer for Pritam and Pedro, and the headline isn't the ATM or the cybercrime or even Warsi's beautifully shabby comic timing. It's the name above the title. Rajkumar Hirani — the filmmaker with a literally perfect record, every one of his films from Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. to 3 Idiots to PK to Sanju a commercial event — is making his streaming debut. The man does not miss. And he has chosen a Goa-set cybercrime comedy to plant his flag on OTT.

"I've always enjoyed stories where very different people are forced to come together and navigate life in unexpected ways. Pritam and Pedro have a lot of humour, warmth and madness in that sense." — Rajkumar Hirani

The setup is pure Hirani: take two men who should never be in the same room and lock them together. Arshad Warsi plays Pedro, an old-school crime branch cop handed a humiliating punishment transfer to the cyber cell — the policing equivalent of being sent to sit in the corner. There he's forced to partner with Pritam, a cocky young hacker played by Vir Hirani, the director's son, making his acting debut in a titular role. (Launching your own kid opposite Arshad Warsi in a show you wrote is either supreme confidence or supreme nepotism, and Hirani has earned enough goodwill that the audience will let him find out which.)

The case that throws them together is gloriously absurd — that mysterious ATM on the beach — and it spirals into a high-stakes international cyber-fraud network with a minister's kidnapped son somewhere in the mix. Standing at the center of the web is Vikrant Massey as Martin, the mastermind. This is the casting that should make you sit up. Massey, fresh off the staggering success of 12th Fail, has spent his career playing the wounded everyman, the boy you root for. Here he's the antagonist — cool, calculating, dangerous. Watching one of the industry's most likeable actors play someone you're supposed to fear is exactly the kind of against-type swing that makes a trailer worth rewatching.

The ensemble is stacked with Hirani regulars and comfort-watch faces: Boman Irani and Mona Singh, both veterans of the Munna Bhai and 3 Idiots universe, plus Satyadeep Mishra and Shruti P Marathe. Behind the camera, Hirani has handed directing duties to Avinash Arun, the cinematographer-turned-director of the gorgeous Killa and Three of Us, who also shot the acclaimed Paatal Lok. It's a smart pairing — Hirani's mainstream warmth filtered through Arun's more textured, atmospheric eye. The Goa in this trailer doesn't look like a postcard. It looks lived-in, a little sweaty, slightly criminal.

"The long-format space gave us the opportunity to spend more time with the characters and really explore their journey," Hirani said of his move to streaming. For a director whose films run on character chemistry above all else, the extended runway of a series could be the best thing that's happened to his storytelling in years.

For the diaspora, the where-to-watch is clean: Pritam and Pedro streams worldwide on JioHotstar from July 3, 2026, which means NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada can stream it the same day it lands in India, no waiting, no torrenting, no asking your cousin in Pune to record it. A JioHotstar subscription is all it takes.

There's a small, lovely meta-joke buried in the marketing — JioHotstar's tagline for the launch reads, "Hackers ki fielding set hai, kyunki Pritam and Pedro are reporting for duty!" It's silly. It's charming. It's deeply Hirani. And after a year of Bollywood box-office anxiety and grim, self-serious thrillers, the prospect of the industry's most reliable feel-good filmmaker showing up on your TV with a clean, funny, heartfelt caper feels like exactly the right kind of homecoming. Mark July 3. Hirani doesn't miss.
